lessons.title: Seem + Adjective
lessons.content: 'Seem' is used with adjectives to describe how someone or something appears. The structure is Subject + seem + Adjective.

details.explanation: 'Seem' is used with adjectives to describe how someone appears.
With third person singular subjects (he, she, it), 'seem' becomes 'seems'.
details.burmese: သူ ကောင်းနပါရတယ်။

lessons.title: Seem to + V1
lessons.content: 'Seem to' is used before a verb infinitive to express how something appears to happen. The structure is Subject + seem to + V1.

details.explanation: 'Seem to' is used before a verb to express how something appears to happen.
details.burmese: မင်း အဲဒီကို သိပါရတယ်။

details.explanation: In negatives, 'doesn't seem to' is used with third person singular subjects.
details.example: She doesn't seem to work there.
details.burmese: သူမ အမှန် အလုပ်လုပ်ပုံ မပေါ်ဘူး။

details.explanation: 'Don't seem to' is used with plural subjects in negatives.
details.example: They don't seem to recognize me.
